description:
Every other planet was spotted by someone looking through a telescope. Neptune was found because astronomers calculated exactly where it had to be before anyone pointed a telescope at it. It remains the only planet discovered by prediction rather than direct observation.

The clue was Uranus. Its orbit kept drifting slightly off from where the mathematics of gravity said it should be, as if something unseen was tugging on it. French mathematician Urbain Le Verrier worked out the position of a planet that would explain the drift. English astronomer John Couch Adams reached a similar answer independently, but his calculation went unpublished.

Adams and Le Verrier's competing claims to the discovery turned into a genuine dispute between Britain and France over who deserved the credit, one that took years to settle into the shared recognition both men now receive.
